name: WorkerBootstrapPlatform::bootstrap_tree

test_list.description: For a live owned process tree, write the secret bytes exactly once with no terminator, keep stdin open after success, and allow a later graceful stop.
After a successful bootstrap, a second bootstrap request fails without writing additional bytes; a child fixture records any unexpected second prefix.
An unknown handle or mismatched root PID is rejected before child stdin is accessed and does not affect the valid owned process.
A timeout covering child-lock acquisition records a terminal force-stop request, kills the worker once the lock becomes available, and lets supervision observe its exit.
Dropping a pending bootstrap future while another operation holds the child lock preserves force-stop intent, kills the worker after lock release, and lets supervision observe its exit.

A synchronous kill request reports pending/unconfirmed termination when the retained child lock is held, while owned async cleanup kills the process after lock release and supervision observes its exit.
Secrets outside the inclusive 1..=4096 byte bound fail with content-free errors, do not write to stdin, and leave a healthy process running.
A credential at the inclusive upper bound is transferred exactly and leaves stdin open while the worker remains live.
Zero or timer-range-overflow deadlines fail before the one-shot attempt is claimed and leave the process healthy.

inputs.name: tree
inputs.description: Opaque retained handle for the process tree to bootstrap.

inputs.name: secret
inputs.description: Credential written exactly as supplied to the retained child's stdin.

inputs.name: timeout
inputs.description: Deadline covering process-lock acquisition and the complete stdin write.

output_description: Success after the bounded exact-prefix write; errors contain no supplied secret bytes. Invalid input and duplicate attempts preserve a healthy process; timeout, write failure, or cancellation after attempt claim persist a force-stop request.
summary: Provide an opt-in SDK platform capability that securely bootstraps a retained worker process over stdin.
